revision_notes: Original source URL (https://dlapiper) was incomplete and could not be verified. Confirmed via Togo's data protection law (Loi n° 2019-014 du 29 octobre 2019 relative à la protection des données à caractère personnel), which regulates cross-border transfers (requiring adequate protection or authorisation from the data protection authority, IPDCP) but does not require that data be stored within national borders. Score of 1 (No data localisation requirements) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Togo has no dedicated data localisation law. Law No. 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on the protection of personal data regulates the collection, processing, storage and transfer of personal data, and requires that cross-border transfers to third countries have an adequate level of protection or prior authorisation from the data protection authority (IPDCP, not yet fully operational), but it does not mandate that data be physically stored within Togo.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check surfaced substantive, multi-source evidence, so the row was moved to the full path. Togo has a growing but still nascent startup ecosystem: trackers record 337+ startups, of which around 47 have raised external funding; venture funding has occurred in most years since 2020 (from a $0.5m pre-seed in 2020 to Gozem's $30m Series B in February 2025 and a further $15m raised later in 2025); several hubs are active (Djanta Tech Hub, WoeLab, PAPRICAI) and a founder consortium (TogoTech) launched in October 2025. Annual VC inflows remain well below the $50m threshold for 'Established', but a growing startup base, recurring funding rounds and multiple hubs support 'Developing' (code 3) rather than 'Emerging' (code 2).
revised_comments: Togo's tech startup ecosystem is developing but still nascent. Trackers record over 337 registered startups, of which around 47 have secured external funding, and annual venture investment has occurred in most years since 2020, led by the ride-hailing and super-app company Gozem (a $30m Series B in February 2025 and a further $15m raised later in 2025). Several active hubs support the ecosystem, including Djanta Tech Hub, WoeLab and PAPRICAI, and a startup consortium, TogoTech, launched in October 2025 to federate the sector and advocate for a startup-friendly legal framework. Early-stage capital remains scarce and the investment landscape is still shallow, dominated by development finance institutions rather than private venture capital.
